2027-07-29.title: Saints Martha, Mary and Lazarus
readings: The glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle
How lovely is your dwelling place, Lord, mighty God
I am the resurrection and the life
2027-07-29.alt: Memorial of Sts Martha, Mary and Lazarus, the sister and brother of Bethany and friends of Jesus. Until 2021 the Roman calendar kept only St Martha on 29 July. The first reading is that of the weekday (Week 17, Year I); the Gospel is the proper one, John 11:19–27, with Luke 10:38–42 as the alternative; the weekday Gospel (Matthew 13:47–53) is not used. Mary of Bethany is not to be confused with St Mary Magdalene, whose feast was kept on 22 July. Psalm verses are given in NRSV numbering. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-07-29.verse: Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. Those who believe in me, even though they die, will live, and everyone who lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?”
theo: Moses finishes the work that he began at the foot of Sinai, and the reading says again and again: he did it “as the Lord had commanded Moses.” The tabernacle is set up on the first day of the first month of the second year, a year, almost to the day, after the Exodus. The ark is brought in, the tablets of the covenant are laid inside it, the mercy seat is set above it, and a curtain screens the ark from sight. Then the Lord answers: “the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle. Moses was not able to enter.” God has come to live in the middle of his people, and he is too great to be entered or used. When the cloud lifts, Israel moves; when it stays, Israel stays; and by night “fire was in the cloud.” The Psalm is the song of one who longs for such a house: “My soul longs, indeed it faints for the courts of the Lord... Even the sparrow finds a home, and the swallow a nest for herself... at your altars, O Lord of hosts.” The Church gives us this reading on the day of three friends of Jesus because Bethany was, for him, such a dwelling place: a house where he was welcome.

The proper Gospel of the memorial is from St John. Bethany is “near Jerusalem, some two miles away,” and Lazarus has been dead four days. “Many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary to console them.” When she hears that Jesus is coming, Martha goes out to meet him, while Mary stays at home. Martha is practical and honest, and the Gospels show her often at the centre of things. She says what many of us have said at a graveside: “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.” But she goes on: “even now I know that God will give you whatever you ask of him.” Jesus tells her, “Your brother will rise again.” She answers with the faith of Israel: “I know that he will rise again in the resurrection on the last day.” And Jesus lifts her from a future hope to a present Person: “I am the resurrection and the life. Those who believe in me, even though they die, will live, and everyone who lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?” Her answer is one of the great confessions of the Gospels, like the one Peter gives at Caesarea Philippi: “Yes, Lord, I believe that you are the Messiah, the Son of God, the one coming into the world.” St Luke gives the other well-known scene, the alternative Gospel today: Martha “welcomed him into her home,” and was “distracted by her many tasks,” while Mary “sat at the Lord's feet and listened to what he was saying.” Jesus does not scold Martha for serving, but for being “worried and distracted by many things”: “there is need of only one thing. Mary has chosen the better part, which will not be taken away from her.” In St John's account of the supper at Bethany a week before the Passion, all three are together: “Martha served, and Lazarus was one of those at the table with him. Mary took a pound of costly perfume... The house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume.” Martha serves, Lazarus sits at table as a witness, and Mary anoints. The Church honours them together as a household where Jesus was a friend, since 2021 on one day. Eastern tradition says Lazarus became bishop of Kition in Cyprus, and Western legends place the family in Provence; these are traditions, not Scripture. The Gospels give us the three of them in their home, and that is enough.
outline: Ask: where do you feel most at home with the Lord, and who has made a home for him in your life?
The tabernacle and the glory: God chooses to live among his people.
Martha's honest faith, and Jesus' words that turn a distant hope into a Person.
Serving and listening: Martha and Mary, and the house at Bethany.
“I am the resurrection and the life.”
live: Welcome Jesus into your home today: set aside five minutes at the table or at a window to read a Gospel passage, quietly, as Mary did.
Do one household task today as an act of love for the Lord, and let it be quiet service, without complaint or comparison.
saints: Sts Martha, Mary and Lazarus of Bethany

Friends of Jesus. Martha welcomed him into her home and confessed him as Messiah and Son of God; Mary sat at his feet and anointed him; Lazarus, whom he raised from the dead, never speaks in the Gospels but is a living sign of the resurrection. St Martha is invoked by those who cook, cater and keep house. The Church honours the three together since 2021.
2027-07-29.prayer: Lord Jesus, you were a guest in the home of Martha, Mary and Lazarus, and you wept at the grave of your friend. Be a guest in our homes, and make them places of hospitality, prayer and peace. Teach us Martha's honest faith, Mary's attentive listening and Lazarus's silent witness. You are the resurrection and the life: strengthen our faith and bring our dead into your light. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: At Mass we meet the Lord who “lived among us” (John 1:14), literally who pitched his tent among us. The tabernacle of the old covenant was filled with the glory of the Lord, but no one could enter it; in the Eucharist the same Lord gives himself to be received. Martha's confession, “I believe that you are the Messiah, the Son of God,” is the faith we renew each time we say Amen to the Body of Christ. And his words, “I am the resurrection and the life,” are the promise behind the Mass for the dead and every Christian funeral.

quick: Moses sets up the tabernacle as the Lord commanded, and the cloud covers the tent while the glory of the Lord fills it.
Martha goes out to meet Jesus and confesses: you are the Messiah, the Son of God; Jesus says: I am the resurrection and the life.
Martha, Mary and Lazarus of Bethany are remembered together as friends who gave Jesus a home.
2027-07-29.action: Make a place in your home or in your day to sit quietly with the Lord for ten minutes.
2027-07-29.question: When I am busy with many things, do I make room for the one thing that is necessary?
kidsaint: Martha, Mary and their brother Lazarus lived in a village called Bethany, and Jesus was their friend. He loved to visit. Martha cooked and cleaned and wanted everything to be just right. Mary sat down by Jesus' feet and listened to him. Jesus said to Martha: dear Martha, you are worried about so many things, but Mary has chosen the best part. When Lazarus died, Jesus cried, and then he called Lazarus back to life! Lesson: it is good to help, but we must also take time to sit with Jesus and listen.

family.explain: Jesus visited the house of his friends Martha and Mary. Martha was busy cooking and cleaning, and Mary sat at Jesus' feet to listen. Martha got upset and asked Jesus to tell Mary to help. Jesus said: Martha, you are worried about many things, but only one thing is really important. Mary has chosen the better part. It is good to serve, and it is also good to sit still and listen to Jesus.
family.intention: We thank God for those who cook and care for us at home, and we pray for families who have lost someone they love.
family.ask: Ask: “When do we sit quietly with Jesus? How could we make our evening prayer a time of listening, and not only of saying words?”

illus: In a parish in the hills of Idukki the women who cooked for the feast every year were led by an old woman, Marthamma, who was always on her feet and never sat in church. The young priest once teased her that she had no time for Jesus. She laughed and said: my prayer is the rice. He did not answer. The next year, after the feast, he sat her down in the front pew with a cup of tea and said: now you listen for ten minutes. She wept quietly. The priest said afterwards that he could not tell which of them had learned more. Jesus loves both the cooking and the listening, and does not want us to lose either. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord Jesus, friend of Martha, Mary and Lazarus, come into our homes. Teach us to serve and to listen, and to believe that you are the resurrection and the life. Amen.
share: Moses did everything just as the Lord had commanded him (Exodus 40:16). Where is the Lord asking me to do as he commands, even in small things?
Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died (John 11:21). What have I said to the Lord at a time of loss, and how did he answer?
Mary has chosen the better part (Luke 10:42). What would it mean to make Mary's choice today?
pm.resp: How lovely is your dwelling place, Lord, mighty God.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a home where Christ is welcome and the Word is heard.
For those who cook, clean and care for others at home, often unseen, that their service be honoured.
For those who mourn a brother, sister or friend, that they may hear Jesus say: I am the resurrection and the life.
For the sick and the dying, and for those who accompany them.
For our group, that we may welcome Christ into our homes and listen to him.
pm.close: Father, your Son found a home among friends in Bethany. Give us the faith to welcome him, the love to serve him and the hope of rising with him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, the first reading ends with a great scene: the tent is finished, and the glory of the Lord fills it, so that even Moses cannot go in. God has come to live among his people. And the Psalm sings what every heart wants: How lovely is your dwelling place, O Lord of hosts (Psalm 84:1). Where is God's dwelling place today? In church, yes. But also in a home like the one in Bethany, where Jesus was welcomed.

Today the Church remembers three friends of Jesus: Martha, Mary and Lazarus. We know them as a household. In Luke, Martha welcomed him into her home, and was busy with serving, while Mary sat at his feet to listen. Jesus said: Martha, Martha, you are worried and distracted by many things; there is need of only one thing. Mary has chosen the better part (Luke 10:41–42). He was not scolding the service; he was warning against the worry. We can serve him in a hundred ways, but he also wants us to sit.

In John's Gospel Martha is the one who goes out to meet Jesus when Lazarus has died. She says what we all say: Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died (John 11:21). It is an honest prayer, with a little reproach in it. And Jesus does not rebuke her. He lifts her faith: I am the resurrection and the life. Those who believe in me, even though they die, will live. Do you believe this? And she answers with one of the greatest confessions in the Gospels: Yes, Lord, I believe that you are the Messiah, the Son of God, the one coming into the world (John 11:27).

What a woman! She serves, she argues, she believes. And her brother Lazarus, who never speaks a word in the Gospels, is called out of the tomb. Dear friends, in our homes there are Marthas, Marys and Lazaruses: those who serve, those who pray, and those who say little but are living signs of what Jesus can do. Let us welcome Jesus in. Let us serve with love, listen with attention, and believe in the one who is the resurrection and the life. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus had friends in a village called Bethany: Martha, Mary and their brother Lazarus. When Jesus visited, Martha cooked and cleaned. Mary sat down next to Jesus and listened to him. Jesus said that listening is very special. And when Lazarus died, Jesus cried, because he loved him. Then he called: Lazarus, come out! And Lazarus came alive again! Jesus is stronger than death. Today let us help at home, and let us also sit quietly and listen to Jesus.

intro: Theme: “I am the resurrection and the life.”
The tent where God lives, Martha's faith, and Mary's better part: three friends of Jesus and the home where he was welcome.

sub: The tabernacle set up as the Lord commanded.
The Word pitched his tent among us.
q: Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle.
And the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory, the glory as of a father's only son, full of grace and truth.
points.apply: Visit the Blessed Sacrament this week and say to the Lord: you are here, and I believe it.

sub: Lord, if you had been here.
I know he will rise on the last day.
You are the Messiah, the Son of God.
q: For I know that my Redeemer lives, and that at the last he will stand upon the earth; and after my skin has been thus destroyed, then in my flesh I shall see God.
She said to him, “Yes, Lord, I believe that you are the Messiah, the Son of God, the one coming into the world.”
points.apply: Bring to Jesus, in honest words like Martha's, one loss or sorrow in your life, and then say: I believe.

sub: Martha welcomed him into her home.
q: One thing I asked of the Lord, that will I seek after: to live in the house of the Lord all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the Lord, and to inquire in his temple.
But the Lord answered her, “Martha, Martha, you are worried and distracted by many things; there is need of only one thing. Mary has chosen the better part, which will not be taken away from her.”
points.apply: Put aside ten minutes each day this week, with no distraction, to listen to a Gospel passage.

concl: God's dwelling among his people reaches its fullness in the Word made flesh, who found a home in the house at Bethany.
Martha's faith, Mary's listening and Lazarus's silent witness show how we welcome the Lord who is the resurrection and the life.
2027-07-29.resolve: Welcome Jesus into your home each day this week with ten minutes of quiet listening, and serve one person with love.
